topic: What happens if you stay in a dark room?
title: What total darkness does
hook: What happens if you stay in a dark room?

beats.label: 1 MINUTE
beats.line: Within a minute of lights out, your pupils open wide to grab more light.

beats.label: 10 MINUTES
beats.line: After ten minutes, the rod cells in your eyes take over the night shift.

beats.label: 15 MINUTES
beats.line: After fifteen minutes in dark silence, some people see faces that aren't there.

beats.label: 30 MINUTES
beats.line: After about thirty minutes, your eyes can be ten thousand times more sensitive.

end.line: Could you last an hour in total darkness?

description: Minute by minute: how your pupils, night-vision cells and brain react when the lights go out.

facts.claim: In darkness the pupils dilate within seconds and are fully open in under about a minute; the slow part of dark adaptation happens in the retina.
facts.source: West Texas A&M Univ. (C. Baird, Science Questions: How long does it take our eyes to fully adapt to darkness?) / Webvision

facts.claim: Cones reach their maximum sensitivity after about 9-10 minutes in the dark; after that the rods (night-vision cells) become the most sensitive cells (rod-cone break, roughly 7-10 min).
facts.source: Webvision (Kalloniatis & Luu, Light and Dark Adaptation) / Wikipedia: Adaptation (eye)

facts.claim: UCL study: 19 volunteers spent 15 minutes in a dark, soundproof (anechoic) room; several saw objects or faces that were not there (effect stronger in hallucination-prone people).
facts.source: Mason & Brady, J Nerv Ment Dis 2009 (UCL) / MedicalXpress 2009

facts.claim: Full dark adaptation takes about 20-30 minutes (rods up to ~30-45) and makes the eye roughly 10,000 to 1,000,000 times more sensitive than in daylight; 10,000x is the conservative low end.
